plan.contextChunk: This figure is a plane diagram in which one ellipse is shown against two superimposed coordinate systems. The standard frame consists of thin black double-headed arrows, a horizontal axis labeled x at its right end and a vertical axis labeled y at its top, meeting at the origin. Laid over them is a second pair of orange double-headed axes rotated counterclockwise about that same origin: the one running from lower left to upper right is labeled x', and the one running from lower right to upper left is labeled y'. The ellipse is a dark blue outline centered at the origin and tilted so that its long axis lies along the orange x'-axis and its short axis along the y'-axis; it crosses the black horizontal axis on both sides and extends above and below the black vertical axis. A small curved arc drawn between the positive x-axis and the positive x'-axis marks the rotation and is labeled theta. Neither set of axes carries tick marks or numeric values. Placing both frames on one picture invites a comparison between a point's coordinates in the original system and its coordinates in the rotated one. The figure motivates the treatment of conic equations that contain an xy term, which describe conics turned away from alignment with the coordinate axes.

interactionPlan.concept: Rotating the coordinate axes to align with a conic section's axes eliminates the xy term from its equation, simplifying its mathematical description.

black vertical y-axis with double-headed arrows and label 'y'
orange rotated x'-axis with double-headed arrows and label 'x''
orange rotated y'-axis with double-headed arrows and label 'y''
dark blue ellipse centered at the origin, with its major and minor axes aligned to the orange x' and y' axes
curved angle arc indicating the rotation between the positive x-axis and positive x'-axis, labeled 'theta'
interactive point on the ellipse (appears on click)
dashed projection lines from the point to the black x and y axes (visible on click)
dashed projection lines from the point to the orange x' and y' axes (visible on click)
coordinate readout labels (x, y) and (x', y') for the point (visible on click)
general conic equation in x and y showing the xy term
simplified standard conic equation in x' and y' without the xy term

interactions.label: Rotation angle (theta)
interactions.teaches: Rotating the custom coordinate frame (x', y') along with the ellipse removes the shape's visual tilt relative to its own axes.

interactions.label: Equation format
interactions.teaches: The standard x,y frame results in an equation with an xy cross-term, whereas the rotated x',y' frame aligned with the ellipse yields a much simpler standard equation.
A single physical point on the ellipse has two completely different mathematical descriptions depending on which coordinate frame is used to measure it.

demo_steps.title: A tilted conic
demo_steps.narration: In the standard x-y coordinate system, an ellipse that is tilted requires a complex equation with an xy cross-term to describe its orientation.

demo_steps.title: Rotating the axes
demo_steps.narration: Drag the slider to change the rotation angle theta. The orange x' and y' axes rotate alongside the ellipse, creating a custom coordinate frame tailored to the shape.

demo_steps.title: Simplifying the equation
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the rotated coordinate system removes the xy term. Relative to the x' and y' axes, the ellipse is not tilted, so its equation takes a simple, standard form.

demo_steps.title: Comparing coordinates
demo_steps.narration: Click any point on the ellipse to drop projection lines to both sets of axes. The same location has one set of coordinates in the x-y frame and a different set in the x'-y' frame.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: By defining a new set of coordinate axes that align with a conic's natural orientation, a complicated equation with an xy term can be reduced to a simple standard form.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Center the origin in the view. Draw standard axes in black and rotated axes in a contrasting orange. The ellipse should be styled in dark blue and always stay aligned with the orange axes. Place the 'theta' arc exactly between the positive x and x' axes. Display the two equations in a corner of the canvas, swapping visibility based on the toggle. When the user clicks the ellipse, draw a dot at that location and show two pairs of orthogonal dashed drop-lines: one pair in black dropping to the x,y axes, and one pair in orange dropping to the x',y' axes.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for rotating the coordinate frame by theta: the learner drags theta, the orange x' and y' axes turn with the ellipse while the black x and y axes stay fixed, showing how rotation removes the visual misalignment behind an xy term.
- Toggle between original and rotated equations: the learner switches from the x,y equation with the xy term to the x',y' equation aligned to the ellipse, and the active axes and equation terms highlight together to show why the rotated frame simplifies the conic.
- Click for coordinate comparison at a point: the learner clicks a point on the ellipse, projections to both axis systems appear with two coordinate readouts, making clear that the same point has different coordinates in the two frames.

authoredContext:
Until now, we have looked at equations of conic sections without an xy term, which aligns the graphs with the x- and y-axes. When we add an xy term, we are rotating the conic about the origin. If the x- and y-axes are rotated through an angle, say θ, then every point on the plane may be thought of as having two representations: (x,y) on the Cartesian plane with the original x-axis and y-axis, and (x ′, y ′) on the new plane defined by the new, rotated axes, called the x'-axis and y'-axis. See the figure.

The graph of the rotated ellipse x 2 + y 2 –xy–15=0

An ellipse centered at the origin, aligned with a rotated coordinate system (x', y') that is at an angle θ with respect to the standard (x, y) coordinate system.

We will find the relationships between x and y on the Cartesian plane with x ′ and y ′ on the new rotated plane. See the figure.

evaluation.notes: The figure is structurally very accurate and features excellent interactivity (slider, point projections) to teach coordinate rotation, but the added background grid and overlaid equation box detract from the clean, minimal aesthetic of the original source.
action_items: Remove the static grid lines to match the clean, abstract style of the source image.
Move the equation display box out of the SVG plot area and into the HTML UI panel to prevent it from cluttering the diagram.
Increase the font size of the axis labels (x, y, x', y') and make them bold-italic to better match the visual weight of the source.
Adjust label placement so that 'y' sits exactly at the top tip of the vertical axis and 'x' sits near the rightmost tip, matching the source layout.
